get.summary: Get confirmed crisis incidents near a point
get.description: Returns all **confirmed** incidents whose coverage polygon contains the given coordinates. An incident is confirmed when its confidence score reaches the threshold (≥40 pts) via community reports and votes, or when an admin/first-responder submits a report. Use this endpoint to decide whether a location is inside an active crisis zone and to populate the crisis feed.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude of the point to check (WGS-84).

parameters.name: lng
parameters.description: Longitude of the point to check (WGS-84).

200.description: List of confirmed incidents that spatially contain the given point.

400.description: Missing or non-finite lat/lng query parameters.

get.summary: Get unconfirmed (pending) incidents near a point
get.description: Returns all **unconfirmed** incidents whose coverage polygon contains the given coordinates. Pending incidents have a positive confidence score but have not yet crossed the confirmation threshold. Useful for showing community-submitted reports that are still being validated.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude of the point to check (WGS-84).

parameters.name: lng
parameters.description: Longitude of the point to check (WGS-84).

200.description: List of unconfirmed incidents that spatially contain the given point.

400.description: Missing or non-finite lat/lng query parameters.

post.description:
Submits a community incident report. The system either associates the report with an existing nearby incident of the same type or creates a new one. Each report increases the incident's confidence score based on the reporter's role and trust level:

- **Admin**: +40 pts
- **First Responder**: +30 pts
- **Mod**: +10 pts
- **Regular user**: +5 pts (plus up to +5 pts from trust score)

When the score reaches **40 pts**, the incident is automatically confirmed and affected users receive a `crisis.alert` WebSocket event.

If `lat`/`lng` are omitted, the user's stored profile location is used. A 100-metre radius polygon is created around the point to represent the incident's coverage area.

typeId.description: UUID of the incident type (from GET /api/incident/type).

description.description: Detailed description of what is happening.
description.example: Strong smell of gas between blocks 12 and 14. Residents are evacuating.

lat.description: Latitude of the incident (optional; falls back to the user's stored location).

lng.description: Longitude of the incident (optional; falls back to the user's stored location).

400.description: Invalid request body or no location available for the user.

get.description: Returns the full catalogue of incident types available for reporting. Incident types are global labels created by administrators (e.g. 'Fire', 'Flood', 'Gas Leak'). Sorted alphabetically.

post.description: Creates a new global incident type label. Only administrators and moderators can create types. The label must be unique and is used to categorise incident reports.

403.description: Forbidden — admin or mod role required.

post.summary: Create incidents for an administrative area (Elevated)
post.description:
Authoritative incident creation for admins, moderators, and first responders. Unlike the community `/api/incident` POST, this endpoint:

1. Queries the **Overpass Turbo API** to fetch the real administrative boundary polygon for the given coordinates at the specified granularity level (block, neighborhood, district, or city).
2. Splits the boundary into a grid of smaller sector polygons to allow fine-grained spatial queries.
3. Creates one incident report per sector, each immediately scored with the caller's authority level, often pushing the confidence score past the confirmation threshold right away.
4. Sends `crisis.alert` WebSocket events to all users with a shared crisis location inside the affected area.

If the Overpass API is unavailable or returns no boundary, the system falls back to a single bounding box of the appropriate size centred on the given point.

**Range → admin level mapping**: block=10, neighborhood=9, district=8, city=6.

lat.description: Latitude of the focal point within the affected area (WGS-84).

lng.description: Longitude of the focal point within the affected area (WGS-84).

range.description: Granularity of the affected area. Controls the OSM admin_level queried and the grid step size.

description.example: River overflowing its banks. Residents on the ground floor should evacuate immediately.

201.description: Incidents created for all sectors of the affected area.

sectorsCreated.description: Number of sector polygons that received an incident report.

403.description: Forbidden — admin, mod, or first_responder role required.

put.summary: Vote on an incident (approve or deny)
put.description:
Submits a community vote on an existing incident. Votes adjust the incident's confidence score based on the voter's role and trust level:

**Upvote (approved=true):**
- Admin / First Responder: +10 pts
- Mod: +4 pts
- Regular user: +2 pts (plus up to +3 pts from trust score)

**Downvote (approved=false):**
- Admin / First Responder: −20 pts
- Mod: −3 pts
- Regular user: −2 pts (minus up to −2 pts from trust score)

If the score drops to 0 or below, the incident is automatically deleted. If a newly downvoted confirmed incident drops below 15 pts, it is also deleted. When an unconfirmed incident crosses 40 pts from a vote, it becomes confirmed and affected users receive a `crisis.alert` WebSocket event.

Note: A user cannot both report and vote on the same incident — submitting a downvote removes the reporter's existing report from that incident.

incidentId.description: UUID of the incident to vote on.

approved.description: true to upvote (confirm), false to downvote (deny).

patch.description:
Registers or updates the authenticated user's real-time crisis location. The coordinates must fall inside at least one **confirmed** incident polygon — if the user is not in an active crisis zone the request is rejected with 403.

Once registered, the location is stored in the `user_crisis` table and is visible to other users in the same crisis zone (via `GET /api/user/location`) and to elevated staff (via `GET /api/admin/location`). The initial crisis status is set to `no_response` until the user updates it with `PATCH /api/user/status`.

403.description: The provided coordinates are not inside any active confirmed crisis zone.

get.summary: Get nearby users in your crisis zone
get.description:
Returns all users who have shared their crisis location within `radius` metres of the authenticated user's own stored crisis location. Both the requesting user and the returned users must be inside an active (confirmed) incident polygon — the endpoint returns 403 if the requesting user has not shared their location or is no longer within a confirmed zone.

This is intended for mutual-aid coordination: users can see who is nearby, what their status is, and whether they need help or can offer it.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Search radius in metres. Defaults to 5000 m (5 km).

200.description: List of nearby users with their crisis status and location.

403.description: The user has not shared a crisis location or is not inside an active confirmed crisis zone.

patch.description:
Updates the authenticated user's self-reported crisis status. The user must have previously shared their location via `PATCH /api/user/location` — the request is rejected with 400 if no crisis location entry exists.

Status values:
- `safe` — The user is unharmed and not in immediate danger.
- `need_help` — The user requires assistance.
- `injured` — The user is physically injured.
- `available_to_help` — The user is safe and able to assist others.
- `no_response` — Default state; the user has not yet updated their status.

400.description: User has not shared a crisis location yet.

get.description: Returns the real-time location and crisis status of **all** users who have shared their crisis location, regardless of which incident zone they are in. Available to administrators, moderators, and first responders. Intended for a global crisis dashboard or incident command view.

200.description: All crisis user entries across all active zones.

403.description: Forbidden — admin, mod, or first_responder role required.
